days.subtheme: Proving your worth to people who already decided
days.title: Why You Keep Trying To Prove Your Worth (And Can Stop)
days.featured_quote: You don't have to keep proving what was never in question.
script_lines: You keep trying to prove you're worth being here.
But worth was never something you had to earn.
It was already yours before anyone gave their opinion.
Some people will never see it, and that's not about you.
Their opinion is not a referendum on your value.
You can stop performing for people who already decided.
You were worthy before the applause and after it stops.

days.title: You Are Not Behind — Here's Why That Timeline Lied
days.featured_quote: You are not behind. You are exactly where your story is.
script_lines: Everyone's timeline looks different, even when it looks the same.
You are not behind just because someone else moved faster.
There is no deadline on becoming who you're becoming.
Comparing chapters only tells you where you are, not your worth.
Some things take longer because they're built to last.
You're not late. You're exactly where your story is.
Slow is still moving. Moving still counts.

days.title: Rest Doesn't Require A Good Enough Reason
days.featured_quote: Rest doesn't need a permission slip.
script_lines: Your worth doesn't go up on your productive days.
It doesn't go down on your slow, tired ones either.
You are not a task list wearing a person's name.
Rest doesn't require justification or a good enough reason.
You were worthy before you accomplished a single thing today.
Doing less doesn't make you less.
You get to exist without earning it first.

days.subtheme: The stories you tell yourself about your worth
days.title: The Story You're Telling Yourself About Your Worth Is Editable
days.featured_quote: You're allowed to rewrite the story you've been telling about yourself.
script_lines: The story you tell about yourself becomes the one you live.
Somewhere along the way, you started believing a smaller version.
That story was written by moments, not by facts.
You're allowed to go back and edit the ending.
A different chapter doesn't erase the ones before it.
You get to decide what the next line says.
Your worth was never the plot twist you thought it was.

days.subtheme: Small acts of self-respect build self-worth
days.title: How Self-Worth Is Actually Built, One Small Promise At A Time
days.featured_quote: Self-worth is built the same way trust is — one kept promise at a time.
script_lines: Self-worth isn't a feeling you wait around for.
It's built the same way trust is, one small choice at a time.
Every time you keep a promise to yourself, it grows.
Every boundary you hold adds a little more evidence.
You don't need to feel worthy to start acting like it.
The feeling tends to catch up to the practice.
Small and consistent beats big and occasional every time.

days.subtheme: Comparison and social media's effect on worth
days.title: What Scrolling Is Actually Doing To Your Sense Of Worth
days.featured_quote: Someone else's pace was never proof of your worth.
script_lines: Comparison online moves at a speed real life never does.
You're seeing someone's highlight reel, not their whole footage.
Their timeline was never a fair measure of yours.
The scroll makes you feel behind faster than reality ever could.
You can enjoy someone's win without shrinking your own story.
Their pace was never proof of your worth.
Closing the app doesn't mean you're falling behind.

days.subtheme: Integration: self-worth as an ongoing practice
days.title: Self-Worth Isn't A Destination — It's A Practice
days.featured_quote: You were never behind. You were becoming.
script_lines: Self-worth isn't a destination you arrive at once.
It's a practice you return to, especially on hard days.
You won't feel worthy every single day, and that's human.
The goal isn't constant confidence. It's coming back to yourself.
Every day you chose to be kind to yourself counted.
You are allowed to keep practicing without being perfect at it.
You were never behind. You were becoming.
